fact: MoFPED's monitoring covered IRAS in nine cities, the tenth city, Jinja, still using e-LogRev, in the first half of FY2024/25; the report also says IRAS is being rolled out in all LGs but gives no count.
LG own revenue reached 37 percent of the annual budget at half-year FY2024/25, up from 24.35 percent at half-year of the FY2019/20 baseline, which MoFPED attributes to the IRAS rollout across LGs.

The Auditor General's information systems audit found ELOGREV implemented at only 71 out of 2,366 sites since the 2014/2015 financial year; sites are not the same as local governments, so this is a count of sites.

The ELOGREV contract with Tucksee Pty Limited does not clearly require source code transfer to government, and there is no formal access policy for the database; audit summarised 24 December 2024, undated.
ELOGREV implementation is funded by both MoFPED and URA TREP, which the audit says risks duplicated payments; budgets ignore sites covered by other revenue systems.

The audit says MoLG lacks an IT Strategic Plan, Risk Management Policy and Security Policy, and has no IT steering or strategy committees; it also recommends harmonising ELOGREV rollout with ECITIE and IRAS.

The Independent, citing the IRAS website, says IRAS was rolled out in 98 districts, 21 municipalities and 9 cities (128 local governments) at a cost of UGX 20.07 billion to date; no national total is given. Date is the article's March 2024.
The article says the Ministry of Local Government's E-LogRev was operational in 48 local governments; no total is given. Date is the article's March 2024.

The Auditor General's report on FY2022/23, quoted here, counts 124 activated local governments, 39 of which lacked enough phones, laptops, printers and POS machines to operate the revenue system; no national total is given.

Nansana's mayor says the system fixes assessment so that no assessor discretion enters, helps taxpayers keep records and records payments against a catalogue of fees, with an undefined 'other revenue' line open to under-recording; article of March 2024.

The Ministry of Local Government runs E-LogRev, which the article describes as the ministry's initiative alongside IRAS, introduced from 2017 under the government's automation of local revenue systems.
